claims.head: The Canucks can’t afford to take penalties
claims.call: The Oilers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.7 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Canucks’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Oilers’ power play is the league’s best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Canucks tonight.
claims.nums: Edmonton 1st for power play (9.7 expected goals per 60) · Vancouver 26th for penalty kill
claims.gist: The Oilers’ power play has a soft target in the Canucks’ kill.

claims.head: Quality over quantity for the Oilers
claims.call: The Oilers’ average shot has at least their usual 6.6% chance of going in.
claims.body: The Oilers make their shots count, and the Canucks are one of the league’s worst at preventing dangerous shots. Expect the Oilers to get some real chances.

claims.head: Active D against forward-led
claims.body: The Oilers are one of the league’s best for shots from defensemen, at the active D end; the Canucks are one of the league’s worst, at the forward-led end. Expect that gap to show.
claims.gist: The Oilers and the Canucks sit at opposite ends for shots from defensemen.
claims.call: The Oilers’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Canucks’.

EDM.head: Edmonton has nearly everything going for them
EDM.body: Edmonton has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Anything short of a win would be a surprise, though Vancouver can make a game of it if their power play gets going.

VAN.head: Vancouver has their work cut out
VAN.body: Edmonton has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Vancouver’s best hope is a power play that gets going, plus a big night in goal.

story.head: McDavid’s favourite opponent
paras: The Canucks already came to Edmonton once this season and left with a 6-5 overtime win. The Canucks come in at 1-0-0, the Oilers at 0-0-1.
The Oilers’ power play has a soft target in the Canucks’ kill. The Oilers and the Canucks sit at opposite ends for shots from defensemen.
